source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why is a plausible document title insufficient evidence that a repaired link is correct?

options.text: The saved title is sufficient evidence that the link has the intended target.
options.feedback: A plausible label can point to the wrong document. Reading the destination checks its identity rather than relying on the displayed label.

options.text: The agent's completion claim establishes that the destination was inspected.
options.feedback: A completion sentence is not evidence that inspection occurred. Check the destination content and the actual action evidence.

options.text: Opening a document establishes that the link now reaches the intended reading.
options.feedback: A successful click establishes that a destination opens. You still need to inspect whether that destination contains the intended reading.

options.text: Different documents can appear under the same convincing title.
options.feedback: A label can look appropriate even when the destination is wrong. Open the saved link and confirm that the document itself is the intended one.
